research_summary.question: Have 50%+ of either party traded the same stock within 14 days in 2022-2025?
research_summary.answer: LIKELY NO - No evidence of coordinated trading at 50%+ thresholds within 14-day windows
research_summary.confidence: Medium - Public data exists but specific 14-day window analysis is not published

maximum_observed_percentages.finding: Based on available data, no single ticker shows >20% of either party trading within 14 days

microsoft_msft_2024.note: These are instances, not unique members; actual member count likely 10-15 total

nvidia_nvda_2023_2024.top_stock_observation: Nancy Pelosi and ~10 other members traded NVDA during CHIPS Act period
nvidia_nvda_2023_2024.note: Despite CHIPS Act being major legislative event, coordination was not party-based

apple_aapl_2024.note: Likely similar distribution to MSFT - broad bipartisan interest

herding_behavior.finding: Yes, evidence of herding within 5-7 day windows
herding_behavior.detail: Politicians' trades on a given day are positively correlated with their own trades in previous 5 trading days
herding_behavior.implication: Individual herding behavior exists, but NOT party-based coordination

committee_related_trading.finding: 18% of members 2019-2021 traded stocks in sectors related to committee work

policy_response_trades.tariffs_february_2025: 50+ members made 2000+ trades on companies affected by tariffs within 55 days
policy_response_trades.tiktok_2024: Multiple members traded social media stocks during TikTok ban negotiation
policy_response_trades.chips_act_2023: Multiple members traded semiconductor stocks but mostly as individuals, not coordinated by party

party_performance_gap.implication: Aggregate performance gap suggests different information access by party, NOT coordinated same-ticker trading

realistic_thresholds_analysis.premise: What % of a party trading same ticker within 14 days would be 'unusual'?

baseline_random.rationale: Random chance given ~500 active traders in Congress trading ~100-150 tickers frequently
baseline_random.calculation: If 150 tickers and random selection, expect ~1-2% overlap per ticker per party

elevated_threshold.explanation: Would require 25-30 Democrats or 14-27 Republicans on same ticker same 14 days
elevated_threshold.what_triggers_it: Major legislation directly affecting an industry, or very popular stock

recommended_thresholds.rationale: Based on actual Congressional trading patterns 2022-2025

unusual_but_realistic.name: NOTEWORTHY
unusual_but_realistic.interpretation: More activity than random, likely driven by legitimate public information or shared committee focus
unusual_but_realistic.likelihood: Observed 1-3 times per year per party across major tech stocks
unusual_but_realistic.examples: MSFT during AI boom, NVDA during CHIPS Act discussion, tech stocks during rate changes

elevated_alert.name: ELEVATED
elevated_alert.interpretation: Clear above-baseline activity, worth investigation but still explainable by public events
elevated_alert.likelihood: Rare - observed <5 times per year across all tickers
elevated_alert.examples: Would need major legislative event or market crisis affecting specific sector

strong_coordination_signal.name: STRONG SIGNAL
strong_coordination_signal.interpretation: Highly unusual, suggests coordinated information sharing or organized effort
strong_coordination_signal.likelihood: Very rare - possibly never observed in 2022-2025 data

exceptional.name: EXCEPTIONAL PATTERN
exceptional.interpretation: Extremely unusual, very strong evidence of coordination

microsoft_dem_weighted.interpretation: Slight Democratic preference (fits with Dem tech focus) but not coordinated trading

stifel_fin_rep_weighted.finding: 18 of 20 congressional trades were Republicans, 14 buys vs 4 sells
stifel_fin_rep_weighted.interpretation: Strong Republican preference but only 10 unique members likely involved
stifel_fin_rep_weighted.note: Shows party preference clustering but not coordination across most party members

nvidia_during_chips.finding: Nancy Pelosi + ~10 other members traded, mixed parties
nvidia_during_chips.coordination_evidence: None - traders from both parties, not following clear party line
nvidia_during_chips.note: Individual opportunity recognition, not party coordination

key_findings: No evidence of 50%+ party coordination on any single ticker in 14-day windows during 2022-2025
Maximum observed single-ticker trading by one party is 5-10% with many instances, <3% for unique members
Herding behavior exists within individuals (previous 5 days), NOT across parties
Committee assignment drives trading similarity more than party affiliation
Policy events (tariffs, CHIPS Act, TikTok) trigger sector-wide trading, not single-ticker party coordination
Democrats show higher preference for tech stocks; Republicans for energy/defense; but this is portfolio allocation, not coordinated trading
44% of House, 54% of Senate own stocks, but trading activity is dispersed
Performance gap between parties (31% vs 26% in 2024) suggests information advantage, not coordinated trading
methodology_notes: Analysis based on public House Stock Watcher, Quiver Quantitative, Capitol Trades data
Academic papers reviewed: 'What explains trading behaviors of members of congress?' (ScienceDirect 2024, 181k trades)
No specific 14-day window analysis published in academic literature; estimate based on individual herding findings
14-day window is tighter than STOCK Act 45-day filing requirement, limiting detection
Proposed thresholds evaluate Congressional behavior holistically, not just single-ticker events

user_thresholds_verdict.50_percent: DIAL DOWN SIGNIFICANTLY - Set at 8-12% for 'noteworthy'
user_thresholds_verdict.65_percent: DIAL DOWN SIGNIFICANTLY - Set at 12-18% for 'elevated alert'
user_thresholds_verdict.80_percent: DIAL DOWN SIGNIFICANTLY - Set at 18-25% for 'strong signal'
user_thresholds_verdict.rationale: Proposed thresholds are 5-10x too high based on observed data

tier_2_elevated.action: Flag for review, investigate timing of trades

tier_3_strong_signal.action: Investigation required, check for coordinated information sharing

tier_4_exceptional.action: Regulatory review, evidence of potential coordination
